title: State of Tamil Nadu & Karnataka v. Koose Muniswamy Veerappan (Operation Cocoon)
crime_type: Forest Banditry / Sandalwood Smuggling / Elephant Poaching / Ambush of Police Forces
court_or_authority: Special STF Joint Operations / High Court of Madras
legal_citation: 2004 SCC OnLine Mad 982; Special STF Report No. 44/2004
source: Tamil Nadu Special Task Force Archive & Indian Kanoon
location: Sathyamangalam & MM Hills Forest Ranges, Tamil Nadu & Karnataka, India

suspects.name: Koose Muniswamy Veerappan
suspects.role: Bandit Gang Leader (Killed in STF Ambush)

evidence: Recovery of 12 Bore rifles, self-loading rifles (SLR), hand grenades, and wireless transceivers from ambushed ambulance vehicle
Ballistic matching linking seized weapons to assassination of 184 police officers and forest rangers over three decades
Intelligence audio intercepts of undercover STF operative disguised as arms broker infiltrator
Forensic autopsies of Veerappan and three associates confirming bullet wounds sustained in tactical STF counter-ambush
modus_operandi: Controlled 6,000 sq km of dense scrub jungle across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala. Operated an armed insurgent bandit network harvesting thousands of tons of sandalwood and poaching hundreds of elephants. Kidnapped high-profile dignitaries (including Kannada superstar Dr. Rajkumar) for multi-crore ransom and executed landmine ambushes against police task forces.
personality_disorder: Megalomanic forest insurgent mindset, ruthless guerrilla violence, and predatory mastery of wilderness terrain.
common_traits: Landmine and improvised explosive ambushes of police convoys
Kidnapping public figures and cinema icons for state ransom demands
Ruthless execution of suspected tribal police informants
summary: Operation Cocoon was a 10-month undercover intelligence operation by the Tamil Nadu STF led by K. Vijay Kumar. Infiltrators lured Veerappan out of the jungle in an ambulance on pretext of eye medical surgery, neutralizing the gang in an encounter at Papparapatti.
